blocking.issue: Revision prefix lookup has no REST path to call. The CLI accepts `rev-<12 hex>` as a lookup key for Revision sources, but the REST conventions allow only full digests in paths, and no collection filter or search parameter is defined. So the CLI cannot resolve a prefix, or detect that one is ambiguous, without listing every Revision, and that listing is unbounded.
blocking.evidence: "Read commands accept the display form `rev-<12 hex>` as a lookup key and fail with exit code 2 when it is ambiguous" (Bundle verbs in detail); "| Revision identifier | `rev-162af81f5de4` or `sha256:<64 hex>` | A Revision from Ruralz Control, fetched from `revisions` |"; versus REST conventions: "Digests in paths and bodies are full `sha256:<64 hex>` values"
blocking.fix: Add a lookup to the REST API table, for example `GET /api/v1/revisions?digestPrefix=<12 hex>&environment=NAME`, that returns at most 2 matches, and state that the CLI uses it. Add it as a proposal to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-3, or open a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops. The other option is to require the full `sha256:<64 hex>` for every Revision source and change the worked example (`ruralz bundle diff rev-162af81f5de4 ...`) to match.

blocking.issue: The document does not say how `ruralz test run --bundle` and `ruralz dev run` start a local `ruralzd` for an arbitrary Bundle. Listener ports are required Bundle fields and part of the digest (Configuration model Gateway: `port: 8443 # required`). The admin port defaults to 9901. The only process settings are `RURALZ_CONFIG`, `RURALZ_DATA_DIR` and `RURALZ_LOG_LEVEL`. So there is no way to move listeners to loopback or ephemeral ports without changing the tested Revision. Parallel CI jobs would collide on 8443 and 9901. The `secretRef` values, such as the `file` TLS certificates under `/etc/ruralz/tls`, would not resolve on a CI runner, so `/readyz` never turns 200. File-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay (the OQ-configuration-model-10 decision), yet `dev run --env` promises Hot Reload of an overlaid render, and the re-render and watch loop is not described.
blocking.evidence: "With `--bundle DIR`, `ruralz test run` starts a local `ruralzd` on loopback ports with that Bundle rendered for `--env`"; "| `ruralz dev run` | Launch a local `ruralzd` on a Bundle directory with Hot Reload | `[DIR]`, `--env`, `--environments` | Local `ruralzd` |"
blocking.fix: Add a subsection, "Local ruralzd launched by the CLI", that states: (1) how listener and admin ports are rebound, either as a CLI-only render transform whose digest is reported as a test digest that differs from the Revision, or through a proposed `RURALZ_*` listener and admin override setting, recorded in a new OQ-cli-and-api-surface-N that needs a pack section 2 amendment; (2) how `secretRef` values are satisfied locally, for example a `--secret-overrides FILE` mapping, or a documented failure with RZ-CFG-026 and exit 2; (3) that the CLI waits for `/readyz` on the chosen admin port with a bounded timeout (target); (4) that `dev run --env` re-renders on change to a temporary rendered file, which it replaces atomically for Hot Reload.

blocking.issue: The document claims a single CLI for Linux, macOS and Windows but does not say which commands work where. That contradicts the tech stack platform table. `ruralzd` and `ruralz-control` are "Not planned: no production target" on windows/amd64 and "Development only" on darwin, and Windows has no SIGTERM. On Windows, `ruralz dev run`, `ruralz test run --bundle`, `ruralz node drain`, `ruralz control serve` and `ruralz control restore` therefore cannot work as written.
blocking.evidence: "The CLI is one static binary, `ruralz`, built with `CGO_ENABLED=0` for Linux, macOS and Windows." and "`ruralz dev run` and `ruralz test run` launch a local `ruralzd` binary"; Tech stack and libraries, Static builds: "| windows/amd64 | Not planned: no production target | Not planned: no production target | Production (CLI) |"
blocking.fix: Add a platform column or a short table that marks these commands "Not planned on Windows: no `ruralzd` or `ruralz-control` build", and marks darwin "development only" for `dev run` and `test run --bundle`. On unsupported platforms the commands exit 2 with a clear message. Point `test run` users on Windows to `--target URL`.

blocking.issue: The document does not say how `ruralz node drain` finds the process to signal. A file lock taken with flock has no queryable owner PID. System overview says the old process releases the lock at Drain start, so during a Zero-Downtime Upgrade the lock holder changes. The CLI and a containerized `ruralzd` usually live in different PID namespaces, and signaling another user's process needs privileges. The command table defines no PID source, and the text does not cover a lock that no process holds, or one that changes owner while `--timeout` waits.
blocking.evidence: "on the Node's host it sends SIGTERM to the `ruralzd` process holding the file lock on `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, starting a Drain as a process manager would ([ADR-0015](...)), and waits for exit or `--timeout`"; the table lists only "`--data-dir PATH` (default `RURALZ_DATA_DIR`), `--timeout DURATION` | Local process signal"
blocking.fix: Specify the mechanism, for example a PID and start-time record that the lock holder writes under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` (layout owned by Data plane). The CLI then verifies the record against the lock (for example a POSIX `F_OFD_GETLK` or `/proc/locks` check on Linux) before it signals. Define exit 2 for no holder, a stale record or permission denied, and state that the command signals only the process recorded at invocation. In Kubernetes or systemd, send operators to Pod deletion or `systemctl stop` instead. Record the Linux-only limit, and leave the remote case to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-4.

blocking.issue: `ruralz control join` cannot be built as specified. Joining a replica needs a key pair on the new replica's host, a certificate stored in that replica's data directory, and a pinned server CA for the first TLS dial. The command has no data directory, no key or output location and no pin input, and the global `--ca-file` covers only 8090 and 9901. Security and identity describes `Join` as sent "from a replica without a peer certificate" over a pinned server CA, so it is not clear whether the CLI or the replica process dials 8092, or where the private key is created.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz control join` | Join a replica to the Raft cluster by redeeming a one-time `admin` token | `--peer HOST:8092`, `--token-file PATH` | Peer layer 8092 `Join` |"; Figure 3: "cli -.->|\"control join\"| peer"; Security and identity transport table: "except token `Join` from a replica without a peer certificate ... `Join` redeems a one-time `admin` token over a pinned server CA"
blocking.fix: Define `ruralz control join` as acting on the local replica's data directory: add a `--data-dir PATH` flag (required). The replica key is generated there, and the certificate chain and peer CA are written there. State that the join token embeds the SHA-256 fingerprint of the 8092 server CA, as Enrollment tokens do, and that the CLI refuses an unpinned dial. Alternatively, make `join` a mode of `ruralz control serve` (`-- --join HOST:8092 --join-token-file PATH`) and update Figure 3 and the Surface column.

blocking.issue: `ruralz control restore` cannot run in the order given. It needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key. That key's private half must already exist in the restored deployment when the offline root signs the set, but restore targets an empty deployment and has no input for the private key, and no step that generates it and exports its public half. The backup is also "encrypted and signed" (Control plane and GitOps), yet restore takes no decryption key. The Control Store data directory it writes to is not named either.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz control restore` | Restore a Control Store snapshot into an empty deployment | `FILE`, `--anchor-set PATH` (required), `--revocation-list PATH` | Local Control Store |" and "requires a root-signed anchor set so that the restored Ruralz Control opens a higher `storeEpoch` before any delivery"
blocking.fix: Make restore two-step, or add flags. For example, `ruralz control restore --prepare --data-dir PATH` generates the new online key encrypted under the key-encryption key and prints its public half for offline root signing. Then `ruralz control restore FILE --data-dir PATH --anchor-set PATH --backup-key-file PATH [--revocation-list PATH]`. Name where the backup encryption key comes from, or add an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

blocking.issue: `--wait` can block forever. `paused` is not terminal, and failures under `autoRollback: false` enter `paused` and wait for a human. `--timeout` has no default, so a CI job running `ruralz rollout status --wait` without `--timeout` never exits. The exit code table has no row for `paused`. The polling interval is not stated, so the REST API load from many waiting CI jobs is unbounded.
blocking.evidence: "`ruralz rollout status --wait` polls until the Rollout is terminal."; exit code 1 row: "`rollout status --wait` ended in `rolled-back` or `failed`"; command row: "`CLUSTER` or `ROLLOUT_ID`, `--wait`, `--timeout DURATION`, `--output json`"
blocking.fix: Treat `paused` as a stop condition for `--wait`: exit 1 with the pause reason, or add a `--wait-through-pause` flag. Give `--timeout` a default, for example 60m (target). State a polling interval with backoff, for example 5 s rising to 30 s (target), that honors `Retry-After` on `RZ-CP-010`. Add `paused` to the exit code table.

blocking.issue: The API has no way to approve a revert. Control plane and GitOps says a revert to an older target, or one with `security` impact or a Capability grant, "gets `RZ-CP-006` until another `approver` approves". Here, `ruralz rollout approve` and REST `promotions/{id}/approve` cover only queued promotion records, and `rollouts` has no approve action. The document also does not say whether `ruralz rollout start` then leaves a pending Rollout or fails with exit 2.
blocking.evidence: "Rollouts normally start from promotions; `ruralz rollout start` serves reverts, which need an `operator` with step-up TOTP"; "| `ruralz rollout approve` | Approve a queued promotion when `Environment.spec.promotion.requireApproval` is set | `--env NAME`, `--digest sha256:DIGEST` ...| REST API `promotions` |"; REST row "`/api/v1/rollouts`, `/api/v1/rollouts/{id}` with actions `/pause`, `/resume`, `/rollback`"
blocking.fix: Add a `/approve` action to `/api/v1/rollouts/{id}` with role `approver` and step-up, plus a matching `ruralz rollout approve --rollout ROLLOUT_ID --digest sha256:DIGEST`. State that `ruralz rollout start` prints the Rollout ID and exits 0 while the Rollout waits in `pending` for approval, or exits with a documented code. Alternatively, open an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

blocking.issue: The document uses `ruralz bundle render --api-version` as the apiVersion migration tool, but render merges one overlay and substitutes `${VAR}`: without `--env`, values come from the process environment, and unset variables without a default are RZ-CFG-010. Its output is a one-file rendered Bundle that cannot replace a source tree with `overlays/<env>/` and `${VAR}` expressions. The OQ-configuration-model-7 decision rests on the claim that only comments are lost and that "its diff is empty by construction". That holds only for a rendered Bundle, not for migrating sources.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz bundle render` | Render for one Environment into a one-file Bundle; ... `--api-version` converts |" and "`ruralz bundle render --api-version ruralz/v1beta1` drops comments. For OQ-configuration-model-7 this document chooses option (a), accept the loss: conversion is rare, its diff is empty by construction"
blocking.fix: Specify that `--api-version` switches render into a source-conversion mode. In that mode it converts each base and overlay file in place (with `--output-dir DIR`), skips overlay merge and `${VAR}` substitution, and keeps file layout. Verify the result by rendering both trees for every Environment in `--environments` and requiring an empty `ruralz bundle diff`. If that mode is not wanted, reopen OQ-configuration-model-7 with the real loss stated: overlays, variables, file layout and comments.

non_blocking.suggestion: `ruralz dev tap --route` filters on the client side, so the Node pays about 2 µs per event (target) for every sampled Route. Observability also caps `/tap` at 4 subscribers of 1 MiB each (target) and drops slow events (`ruralz_tap_events_dropped_total`). State the cap, what `dev tap` does when refused (exit 2) or when events are dropped (warn on stderr), and add an Open question for a server-side route filter on `/tap`.

non_blocking.section: Ruralz Control REST and gRPC APIs
non_blocking.suggestion: The gRPC table lists "Renewal" as a row beside `Enroll` and `Stream`, but Release, versioning and compatibility names only the RPCs `Enroll` and `Stream`. State that `RenewRequest` and `RenewResponse` travel on `Stream`, or list the RPC name that Control plane and GitOps defines.

Control plane and GitOps (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-25) relies on a "CLI default" size limit that `ruralz bundle build` enforces. State the defaults from the Configuration model, 64 MiB of source and 20,000 resources (target), and say how the CLI configures them (flag or Open question).

`ruralz ai cost` reads access log records, but Observability says busy Nodes SHOULD set an errors-only `accessLog.when`. That silently drops successful AI requests from cost totals. Either require AI usage records to be logged regardless of `when`, or have `ai cost` warn when records are filtered, and note this in OQ-cli-and-api-surface-6.

With a terminal, `ruralz rollout approve` should also send the digest it displayed, so that a record replaced between display and confirmation is refused. Today only the non-terminal path requires `--digest`.

Tech stack and libraries names the CLI reference as the owner of OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-18 (CLI framework), but this document lists it as a non-goal. Either carry it in the Open questions table with this document as owner, or state that ownership stays with the tech stack document.

"Admin paths never change configuration or Node state" is true, but a leaked operator token can still degrade a Node through CPU profiles and `/tap`. Heap profiles from `/debug/pprof/` can also hold resolved secrets, which the testing strategy excludes from leak checks. Say so beside the `/config/dump` "secrets omitted" claim.

"The CLI warns when a Node is outside the skew window": neither `/config/dump` nor any other admin path listed here returns the Node's binary version. Name the source, for example a `version` member in `/config/dump`, which would need Data plane agreement, or drop the claim.
The ADR links (0006, 0007, 0015, 0017) are broken until those ADR files exist; the verifier reports them as WARN only. Re-check them when the ADRs land.
